findings.evidence: "The two-point approximation of the mean is E[L] ≈ 0.99 × 0.8 + 0.01 × 5.0 ≈ 0.84 s — looks fine."
findings.issue: The arithmetic 0.99 × 0.8 + 0.01 × 5.0 = 0.792 + 0.050 = 0.842 s, which the text rounds to '≈0.84 s'. The next paragraph then gives three further values: the 'analytic mean of the mixture as specified' at ≈0.848 s and the 'sample mean' at 0.85 s. The display '≈0.84 s' is stated first and prominently as the 'two-point approximation', but 0.842 truncated to two decimals is 0.84, while rounded is 0.84 — so the displayed value is a truncation of 0.842. The text explicitly acknowledges this by giving three values and explaining each, so the arithmetic is correct. However, the '≈0.84 s' label on a value of 0.842 could be read as rounding when it is truncation (the figure on p.126 shows 'mean = 0.85s'). Not a computational error but a presentational inconsistency: the figure displays 0.85 (sample mean) while the prose opens with 0.84 (two-point approximation).
findings.fix_instruction: In the opening sentence of §6.3.1, write '≈0.842 s' or add '(the sample mean, shown in Fig. 6.2, is 0.85 s)' to prevent the reader from thinking 0.84 and 0.85 are the same number.

findings.evidence: "Decode: bandwidth verdict, canonical 8×H100 host (TP = 8) | weight-read bandwidth not binding at this operating point | 700 GB/s < 3.35 TB/s → the shard streams in ~5.2 ms at peak, 21% of the 25 ms TPOT step" and "Decode: required bandwidth, hypothetical single-device aggregate (TPOT ~25 ms) | 5.6 TB/s | 140 GB / 0.025 s"
findings.issue: Table 6-1 (p.131) states for decode: '(b) achieved HBM utilization on the canonical host: 0.70 TB/s ÷ 3.35 TB/s = 20.9% per GPU, so weight-read bandwidth is not binding at the canonical point.' The 20.9% figure (0.70/3.35 = 0.20896) and the 21% figure in Ch 2 (5.2/25 = 0.208) are the same quantity expressed two ways (bandwidth fraction vs time fraction), both correct. However, Table 6-1's 'Resource tell' column for decode case (ii) says 'low-to-moderate HBM util (~21% of 3.35 TB/s)' — reading '~21% of 3.35 TB/s' is ambiguous: it could be read as a rate (0.21 × 3.35 = 0.70 TB/s, correct) or as a utilization percentage of the peak bandwidth (21%, correct). The phrasing is correct but the unit ('% of TB/s') mixes a dimensionless percentage with a rate unit in a way that could confuse. This is minor prose clarity.
findings.fix_instruction: Change '~21% of 3.35 TB/s' to '~21% of peak (0.70 TB/s)' in Table 6-1's Resource tell column.

findings.evidence: "the residual demand is at least ~44.9 PFLOP/s (51.6 × (1 − 0.13) — this assumes the ~13% upper bound is fully achieved, so the true saving is ≤ 13% and the true residual is ≥ 44.9), i.e. ≥ ~16.2 host-equivalents"
findings.issue: 51.6 × 0.87 = 44.89 ≈ 44.9 PFLOP/s. Correct. 44.9/2.769 = 16.22 ≈ 16.2. Correct. The logic is sound: if the ~13% is an upper bound on the cacheable fraction, the actual saving is ≤13%, so residual ≥ 51.6 × 0.87. Arithmetic verified — no defect.

findings.issue: 32 × 164.1 = 5,251.2 GFLOP. Correct. 32 × 24.1 = 771.2. 140 + 771.2 = 911.2 GB ≈ 911 GB. Correct. 5,251.2/911.2 = 5.763 ≈ 5.8 FLOP/byte. Correct. Then: 'it approaches the KV-only asymptote 164.1 ÷ 24.1 ≈ 6.8 FLOP/byte as batch grows'. 164.1/24.1 = 6.81 ≈ 6.8. Correct. Arithmetic verified — no defect.

findings.chapter: Ch. 6 — Measuring What Matters (Fig. 6.2, book p. 126)
findings.evidence: Figure art (rendered PDF p. 150) labels the red vertical line "SLO 2 s (TTFT budget)". The caption on the same page states the line is "the 2 s request-latency line — the p95 TTFT ceiling (Ch 4, Table 4-1 Latency row; Canonical Workload box), not the 1.2 s design budget". Ch. 4 (PDF p. 112-113) states: "The two thresholds are not interchangeable: 1.2 s is the design budget, ≤ 2 s is the p95 ceiling the budget relaxes to, and any pass/fail judgement on a measured distribution is made against the p95 ceiling, not the budget."
findings.issue: The in-figure label identifies the 2 s p95 ceiling as the "TTFT budget", directly contradicting the caption beneath it and the book's load-bearing budget-vs-ceiling convention (1.2 s = design budget; 2 s = p95 pass/fail ceiling). Unlike Fig. 6.1, whose art erratum (the 'concurrency' entry) is explicitly acknowledged in its caption, this art/caption mismatch is not flagged anywhere.
findings.fix_instruction: Change the figure label to "SLO 2 s (p95 TTFT ceiling)" so the art matches the caption and the Ch. 4 convention; optionally add an erratum note in the caption mirroring the treatment given to Fig. 6.1's art erratum.

findings.evidence: Text states: "prefix caching... ~13% of prefill FLOPs (the whole-slot case) is an upper bound... 1,200 prompt + 8,000 per-query retrieved... byte-identical share is at most the fixed system/instruction portion of the ~1,200-token prompt". Later in 6.6: "~13% of prefill work in the canonical workload".
findings.issue: Ambiguity in the calculation of the 13% figure. The text implies the prefix caching saves the prefill of the 1,200 token prompt (which includes the query). If 1,200 is cached out of 9,200 total, the saving is 1,200/9,200 = 13.04%. However, the text says the "8K retrieved block differs per query and the 1,200-token slot carries the query itself". If the query varies, the 1,200 token block is NOT byte-identical across requests unless the system prompt is distinct from the user query. The text earlier (Ch 4) defines 1,200 as "prompt" and 8,000 as "retrieved context". It is unlikely the entire 1,200 token prompt is byte-identical if it contains the user's specific question. If only the system instruction part is cached, the percentage would be much lower. Using 13% assumes the entire 1,200 token input is static, which contradicts the nature of a Q&A prompt.
findings.fix_instruction: Clarify whether the 1,200 "prompt" tokens are static system instructions or dynamic user questions. If dynamic, the prefix caching saving is overstated. Correct the 13% figure or the definition of the cached prefix.
